method: 10-agent comparative audit, one MO2-subsystem/Eidos-crate pair each, file:line evidence both sides

findings.title: ESL-flagged .esp plugins (ESPFE) are wrongly hoisted into the master block
findings.mo2_evidence: pluginlist.cpp:410-438 (fixPluginRelationships) hoists only `hasLightExtension || hasMasterExtension || isMasterFlagged`; same triple guards drag-drop at pluginlist.cpp:1960-1974. isLightFlagged (the header 0x200 flag, pluginlist.cpp:2145) is deliberately NOT in the predicate, so a light-flagged .esp stays in the normal-plugin section - matching the engine, which only hoists master-flagged/.esm/.esl files.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/lib.rs:130-133 `loads_as_master()` returns `self.is_master || self.is_light || is_master_ext(&self.name)`. `is_light` comes from esplugin's `is_light_plugin()` (lib.rs:299-308), which is flag-set OR .esl extension (esplugin-6.1.4/src/plugin.rs:244-257). sort() (lib.rs:222-231) puts every loads_as_master plugin in tier 1, above all normal ESPs.
findings.description: An ESL-flagged .esp ('ESPFE', extremely common in modern Skyrim SE/Fallout 4 setups - most compatibility patches are flagged light to save load-order slots) is treated as a master by Eidos's sort and moved above every regular .esp. MO2 and the game itself keep such plugins in the normal section: the light flag affects only index assignment (FE:xxx), not load position. Eidos therefore silently reorders the user's load order, placing ESPFE patches BEFORE the plugins they patch, so their overrides lose - classic in-game breakage with no error anywhere. Note esplugin's `is_master_file()` already equals MO2's hoist triple for SkyrimSE/FO4/Starfield (master flag OR .esm/.esl extension, esplugin plugin.rs:219-232).
findings.suggested_fix: In `Plugin::loads_as_master()` drop `|| self.is_light`: `self.is_master || is_master_ext(&self.name)` (the extension term keeps the unparseable-header fallback correct). Keep `is_light` only for generate_indexes, which already matches MO2's `hasLightExtension || isLightFlagged` index rule. Add a test: light-flagged .esp sorts in the normal tier but gets an FE: index.

findings.title: PlainList games: disabled plugins re-enable every launch and lose their order (loadorder.txt is write-only)
findings.mo2_evidence: gamebryogameplugins.cpp:236-244 - after reading plugins.txt, every plugin NOT listed as active is explicitly set STATE_INACTIVE; :241-245 - if plugins.txt is missing/empty, ALL plugins are set inactive. Order comes from loadorder.txt (readLoadOrderList :144-166) with mtime reconciliation against plugins.txt (:43-58), so inactive plugins keep their position.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/loadorder.rs:94-98 - for PlainList, read_active() yields only `(name, true)` pairs (plugins.txt holds active names only); loadorder.rs:108-121 - apply_active() only updates plugins present in that set and sorts unlisted ones to the end (pos usize::MAX); loadorder.rs:71-76 - loadorder.txt is written but never read anywhere in the crate; discover defaults enabled:true (lib.rs:183).
findings.description: For Skyrim LE / Fallout 3 / FNV, plugins.txt is the only thing Eidos reads back (eidos/src/main.rs:46, eidos-gui/src/main.rs:1230), and for these games it lists only ACTIVE plugins. A plugin the user disabled is absent from the file, so on the next prepare_plugins cycle discover() re-creates it enabled:true, apply_active() never touches it, and it is re-activated and re-written - disabling a plugin is literally impossible to persist for these games. Its load-order position is also discarded (dumped to the end). MO2 avoids both problems by treating loadorder.txt as the full-order authority and explicitly marking unlisted plugins inactive.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror GamebryoGamePlugins::readPluginLists: read loadorder.txt (full order) for ordering, plugins.txt for the active set; after applying the active set, mark every discovered non-primary plugin that plugins.txt did not list active as disabled (when the file exists and is non-empty). Optionally compare mtimes to prefer plugins.txt order when it is newer, like MO2's m_LastRead reconciliation.

findings.title: Newly seen plugins default to enabled; MO2 defaults them to inactive
findings.mo2_evidence: pluginlist.cpp:2133 - ESPInfo constructor initializes `enabled(forceLoaded)`, i.e. disabled unless a force-loaded primary; creationgameplugins.cpp:171-175 and gamebryogameplugins.cpp:236-244 then set every plugin not found in plugins.txt to STATE_INACTIVE. Net effect: a freshly installed plugin shows up unchecked.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/lib.rs:179-190 - discover() creates every plugin with `enabled: true` (line 183); loadorder.rs:108-121 - apply_active() leaves plugins absent from the saved set at that default; eidos/src/main.rs:42-50 then writes them as active right before launch.
findings.description: Install a mod with 12 plugins and hit Play: Eidos silently activates all 12 (asterisk games included - they are not in the saved plugins.txt yet, so apply_active skips them). MO2's contract is the opposite: new plugins appear inactive until the user checks them, which protects against optional/FOMOD-leftover plugins, alternate versions shipped side by side, and plugins whose masters are not active. Combined with finding 2 this is the same root cause (default true + no 'unlisted means inactive' pass), but it bites asterisk games too, on every new mod install and on first run.
findings.suggested_fix: Default `enabled` to false in discover() except for spec.primary_plugins (MO2's forceLoaded equivalent); keep apply_active as the thing that turns saved actives on. Surface newly-seen plugins in the GUI instead of auto-enabling.

findings.title: plugins.txt written/read as UTF-8 instead of the Windows ANSI codepage; non-UTF-8 file silently nukes saved state
findings.mo2_evidence: gamebryogameplugins.cpp:97-99 - plugins.txt is encoded with QStringConverter::Encoding::System (Windows ANSI) and only loadorder.txt with Utf8; creationgameplugins.cpp:44 same System encoding for plugins.txt; both write CRLF (:104, :49) and report un-encodable names as errors (:118-121, :73-76). Reads decode with the System encoder too (gamebryogameplugins.cpp:227-228, creationgameplugins.cpp:140-141).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/loadorder.rs:48-76 - write_load_order builds Rust Strings and fs::write()s them, i.e. UTF-8 with bare \n, for both files; loadorder.rs:84-86 - read_active uses fs::read_to_string, which errors on any non-UTF-8 byte and is mapped to 'return empty Vec'.
findings.description: The Creation/Gamebryo engines read plugins.txt with the ANSI codepage (CP1252 under Wine/Proton for Western locales). A plugin with a non-ASCII name (accented French/German mod names are not rare) written as UTF-8 will not match any filename when the game decodes it as CP1252 - the plugin is silently skipped, exactly the failure MO2's System encoding + invalid-name error exists to prevent. The read side is worse: a plugins.txt previously written by MO2/the game containing one CP1252 byte makes read_to_string fail, read_active returns empty, apply_active is skipped (eidos/src/main.rs:47), and with discover's enabled:true default the user's whole active set is silently replaced by 'everything on'.
findings.suggested_fix: Encode plugins.txt as Windows-1252 (encoding_rs) with CRLF and surface an error for unmappable names, keep loadorder.txt UTF-8 like MO2; on read, fall back to WINDOWS_1252 decoding when UTF-8 fails instead of discarding the file.

findings.title: .esl files are not force-disabled on games without light-plugin support
findings.mo2_evidence: pluginlist.cpp:262-264 - in refresh(): `if (!lightPluginsAreSupported && filename.endsWith(".esl")) forceDisabled = true;` so an .esl in a Skyrim LE / FO3 / FNV Data dir can never be activated.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/lib.rs:24-27 - is_plugin() accepts .esl for every game; discover() enables it (lib.rs:183); generate_indexes() with light_ok=false falls into the normal-index branch (lib.rs:259-262), consuming a normal FF-space slot; write_load_order then lists it as active for the plain-list game.
findings.description: On a game whose engine cannot load light plugins (esplugin: supports_light_plugins false for Skyrim LE/FO3/FNV), an .esl that ends up in a mod is discovered, enabled by default, given a sequential normal index (shifting every later plugin's displayed index), and written into plugins.txt. MO2 hard-disables these so they can never pollute the list. Rare, but the failure is confusing: the displayed indexes stop matching what the game actually assigns.
findings.suggested_fix: In discover()/refresh(), when !spec.light_supported() and the name has an .esl extension, force enabled=false (and ideally a force_disabled flag the GUI can't toggle), mirroring MO2's forceDisabled.

findings.title: Non-atomic plugins.txt writes and no empty-list guard
findings.mo2_evidence: gamebryogameplugins.cpp:95 - writes go through SafeWriteFile (temp + commit); :136-141 - if zero plugins were written it logs 'plugin list would be empty, this is almost certainly wrong' and does NOT commit; :26-29 - writePluginLists also refuses to write before the lists were ever read (m_LastRead guard against clobbering state with an uninitialized list).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/loadorder.rs:69 and :76 - fs::write() truncates plugins.txt/loadorder.txt in place, unconditionally, even when self.plugins is empty (header-only file).
findings.description: A crash or ENOSPC mid-write leaves a truncated plugins.txt the game will happily load (= half the mods off); and any caller bug that produces an empty PluginList (e.g. data dir momentarily unreadable - discover() swallows read_dir errors at lib.rs:152) wipes the user's real load order with a header-only file. MO2 defends against both, and its empty-file check is also what its readers use to detect a broken plugins.txt (gamebryogameplugins.cpp:214-218).
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a sibling temp file and rename() over the target; skip the write (with a warning) when no plugin lines would be written, like MO2's writtenCount==0 guard.

findings.title: Existing destination mod dir is a hard error; MO2 offers merge/replace/rename with backup
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/installationmanager.cpp:376-464 (testOverwrite): when mods/<name> exists, a QueryOverwriteDialog offers MERGE (extract over existing files), REPLACE (delete contents but preserve the original meta.ini bytes, lines 426-448, and emit modReplaced for the old installationFile), RENAME (prompt for a new name), or cancel, each with an optional backup copy named <dir>_backup / _backup2... (generateBackupName, :361-374). doInstall (:536-541) additionally keeps the higher version on merge and clears [installedFiles] on non-merge (:556-563).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:140-143 (install_archive) and :394-397 (finish_fomod) return InstallError::Exists whenever mods/<name> is non-empty; the GUI just shows "Install failed: target already exists" (crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:471-475) and the CLI prints the same error (crates/eidos/src/main.rs:401). No merge, replace, rename or backup path exists.
findings.description: Reinstalling or updating any mod (the single most common install after the first one - a new version of an installed mod produces the same guessed name) dead-ends with an error and forces the user to manually delete the mod directory, losing meta.ini (endorsement state, modid, category) in the process. MO2 treats this as a first-class flow: replace preserves meta.ini, merge layers the new files over, and both can snapshot a _backup copy first.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an overwrite policy parameter to install_archive/finish_fomod (Replace | Merge | Rename(new) | Fail) and surface a chooser in the GUI when Exists fires. At minimum implement Replace MO2-style: read meta.ini bytes, remove the dir contents, recreate, restore meta.ini, then install (then write_meta merges sidecar values over it). Add generate_backup_name(dir) -> dir_backup/_backupN and copy the old dir before replacing when a 'keep backup' option is set. For Merge, extract over the existing tree and only bump version when the new one is >= the old.

findings.title: No DataText layer support: 'Data/ + readme.txt' archives fail as NotSimple where MO2 installs them
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_quick/src/installerquick.cpp:66-91 (isDataTextArchiveTopLayer): a level with exactly one directory named like the game's data dir ("Data") plus only txt/pdf/md/jpg/jpeg/png/bmp files is accepted; :101-103 it is checked alongside dataLooksValid inside the getSimpleArchiveBase descent loop, and :152-157 on install the loose doc files are merged into the Data dir, which becomes the install root.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/lib.rs:135-153 (simple_archive_base) only accepts a level via data_looks_valid() or descends through single_subdir() (:99-107), which requires the level to contain exactly ONE entry. A top level of [Data/, readme.txt] has 2 entries and no known folder/extension, so simple_archive_base returns None and install_archive errors with NotSimple (install.rs:156-172).
findings.description: Archives packaged as a Data folder plus a readme/screenshot at the top level - a common Nexus layout - install silently in MO2 (docs end up inside the mod) but hard-fail in Eidos with 'not a simple archive; manual install needed'. Note also that the descent itself is stricter than MO2's: MO2 descends when size()==1 even past a wrapper that contains only a Data dir plus docs one level down (the check runs at every level of the loop).
findings.suggested_fix: Port isDataTextArchiveTopLayer into ArchiveTree (parameterized by the game's data dir name, "Data" for all current Gamebryo targets): exactly one dir case-insensitively equal to the data dir name, >=1 files, all files with extensions in {txt, pdf, md, jpg, jpeg, png, bmp}. Check it next to data_looks_valid in simple_archive_base's loop, and have install_archive use <prefix>/Data as the move source while also moving the sibling doc files into the destination (MO2 merges them into the Data tree).

findings.title: guess_mod_name keeps the whole Nexus suffix (mod id included) when any version segment has a letter, and never extracts the mod ID
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/nexusinterface.cpp:332-357 (interpretNexusFileName): the 'complex' regex captures the name before '-<modid>-' and lets '.*?' swallow the ENTIRE rest of the filename, so lettered version segments ('4-2-9b', '5-2SE', explicit '[ab]?' in the version group) are stripped, and group 3 yields the Nexus mod ID; installationmanager.cpp:704-717 uses that ID (modID = guessedModID when no sidecar) and it lands in meta.ini as modid (:533-535).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/lib.rs:217-236 (guess_mod_name) pops trailing '-' groups only while they are ALL-ASCII-digits, stopping at the first non-digit segment, and extracts no mod ID. Verified: 'Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch-266-4-2-9b-1700000000.7z' -> 'Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch-266-4-2-9b' (MO2: 'Unofficial Skyrim Special Edition Patch', modID 266); 'SkyUI_5_2_SE-12604-5-2SE.7z' -> 'SkyUI_5_2_SE-12604-5-2SE' (MO2: 'SkyUI_5_2_SE', modID 12604).
findings.description: Nexus uploaders routinely use lettered version components (beta/hotfix suffixes like 1-2a, 9b, 2SE). For every such file the digit-popping heuristic bails immediately, so the mod directory is named with the full '-<modid>-<version>' garbage attached - worse than MO2 on exactly the files the docstring claims to mirror. Separately, because the ID is never parsed, a manually-downloaded Nexus archive (no .meta sidecar) gets no modid in meta.ini (install.rs:198-200 only reads the sidecar), which permanently disables Nexus update checks for that mod.
findings.suggested_fix: Port the complex regex: ^([A-Za-z0-9_'"\-.() ]*?)([-_ ][VvRr]+[0-9]+(...)?[ab]?)??-([1-9][0-9]+)?-.*?\.(zip|rar|7z)$ - returning (name, Option<mod_id>). Fall back to the current digit-popping for non-matching names. Thread the guessed mod id into install_archive/write_meta so modid is seeded when the sidecar is absent.

findings.title: Sidecar modName is ignored when naming the mod; MO2 gives meta names precedence over the filename guess
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/installationmanager.cpp:660-663: modName.update(name-from-.meta, GUESS_FALLBACK) and modName.update(modName-from-.meta, GUESS_META); :716 updates the filename guess only at GUESS_GOOD. uibase/include/uibase/guessedvalue.h:36-45,242-246: META(3) > GOOD(2) and update() only replaces at quality >= current, so the sidecar's modName wins for every managed download.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:463 and crates/eidos/src/main.rs:400 derive the name exclusively via eidos_install::guess_mod_name(filename). install.rs:189-216 (write_meta) reads the sidecar but only after the directory name was already chosen, and ModMeta has no modName accessor (crates/eidos-instance/src/meta.rs). Yet Eidos's own download pipeline writes modName= into every sidecar (crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:284).
findings.description: For downloads made through Eidos's own Nexus integration, the authoritative mod name is sitting in the .meta sidecar Eidos wrote, but installs are named from the mangled archive filename instead. MO2 names the same download by the Nexus mod name ('Dynamic String Distributor (DSD)' vs 'Dynamic String Distributor'), so shared instances get differently-named mod dirs depending on which tool installed them, and Eidos loses the author-intended name for free.
findings.suggested_fix: Before falling back to guess_mod_name, read the <archive>.meta sidecar and prefer its modName (then the HTML-stripped name field) - i.e. reproduce MO2's FALLBACK < GOOD < META ladder in a small pick_mod_name(archive) helper used by both GUI and CLI. Run the result through the sanitizer (separate finding).

findings.title: No fixDirectoryName-style sanitization of the mod directory name
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/installationmanager.cpp:639 installs fixDirectoryName as a filter on EVERY name candidate; uibase/src/filesystemutilities.cpp:9-35: simplified() whitespace, strip trailing dots, delete <>:"/\|?*, reject reserved device names (CON, NUL, COM1...), reject empty (re-prompt via ensureValidModName, installationmanager.cpp:466-481).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:140 (mods_dir.join(name)) and :394 use the caller's name verbatim; nothing in eidos-install or the callers sanitizes (grep for sanitize/fix_directory across eidos-install and eidos-gui finds nothing). The CLI even passes a raw user argument (crates/eidos/src/main.rs:400), so `eidos install x.7z "a/b"` silently creates a nested mods/a/b. Verified: 'Awesome Mod Inc.-456-1-0-1700000000.zip' guesses to 'Awesome Mod Inc.' - trailing dot kept.
findings.description: Eidos explicitly targets MO2-compatible instances, and mod names flow from archive filenames (which on Linux may legally contain \ : * ? " < > |) and raw CLI args (which may contain /). Trailing dots/spaces and Windows-invalid characters produce mod dirs that MO2 (or any NTFS-mounted mods dir) cannot open, and a '/' in the name escapes the mods/ root into an unexpected nested path. Adopting the sidecar modName (previous finding) makes this mandatory: real Nexus mod names like 'Beyond Skyrim: Bruma' contain ':'.
findings.suggested_fix: Port fixDirectoryName as fn fix_directory_name(&str) -> Option<String> in eidos-install (collapse whitespace, strip trailing dots/spaces, remove <>:"/\|?* and control chars, reject reserved DOS names and empty results) and apply it inside install_archive/finish_fomod to the name before joining, returning a new InstallError::BadName (or auto-fixing) when it changes to empty.

findings.title: meta.ini seeding gaps: no date-fallback version, no nexusFileStatus, installationFile loses non-downloads paths
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/installationmanager.cpp:699-702: when the sidecar has no version, MO2 writes version = "d" + lastModified "yyyy.M.d"; :549 writes nexusFileStatus from the sidecar's fileCategory (default 1); :719-722 stores installationFile as the bare filename only when the archive is inside the downloads dir, otherwise the absolute path.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:201-203 only writes version when the sidecar provides one (no fallback at all); no nexusFileStatus is written despite eidos-nexus writing fileCategory into sidecars (crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:287-289); :209-211 always stores the bare file name regardless of the archive's location.
findings.description: The missing version fallback has a concrete consequence: ModMeta::update_available (crates/eidos-instance/src/meta.rs:129-134) requires BOTH version and newestVersion, and the update check only sets newestVersion (crates/eidos/src/main.rs:533), so a mod installed from a sidecar-less archive can never show an update badge in Eidos, and MO2 opening the same instance sees a versionless mod it would normally have stamped with the install date. The installationFile divergence means archives installed from outside downloads/ cannot be traced back to their source file the way MO2 does.
findings.suggested_fix: In write_meta: when from.version() is None, write version as "d" + the archive mtime formatted yyyy.M.d (no zero-padding, matching Qt's format); copy the sidecar's fileCategory into nexusFileStatus (default 1); and store the absolute archive path in installationFile unless archive.parent() == the instance downloads dir (pass the downloads dir into install_archive or compare against mods_dir/../downloads).

findings.title: Empty <file>/<folder> source is installed instead of skipped - <folder source=""> copies the whole archive (fomod/ included) into the mod
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:753-762 (readFileList): if attributes.value("source").isEmpty() the entry is dropped with log::debug("Ignoring {} entry with empty source."). The comment explains real FOMODs ship <folder source="" destination=""/> as a no-op option and that installing it would 'copy everything including the fomod directory'.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/parse.rs:81-95 (parse_file_list) keeps items with source="" (unwrap_or("")); crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:258-269 resolve_ci(root, "") returns Some(root) because the split-filter removes all components; install.rs:299-314 apply_plan then runs copy_dir_all(root, dest.join("")) for a folder item - i.e. the entire extraction root including fomod/ is copied into the mod - or fs::copy(root_dir, ...) for a file item, which errors and fails the whole install.
findings.description: FOMOD authors commonly use <folder source="" destination=""/> to make a 'do nothing' option (MO2's source comment documents this). When such an option is selected, Eidos resolves the empty source to the extraction root: a folder item duplicates the entire archive (wrapper dirs, fomod/, all unselected variants) into the installed mod; a file item aborts the install with an Io error. MO2 simply ignores entries with an empty source.
findings.suggested_fix: In parse_file_list (parse.rs), skip <file>/<folder> entries whose source attribute is empty/whitespace, mirroring MO2's readFileList. Alternatively (or additionally) guard in apply_plan: if item.source is empty, continue.

findings.title: Empty (or trailing-slash) file destination fails the install instead of using the source filename
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:310-313 (copyLeaf): if destinationPath.isEmpty() || endsWith("/") || endsWith("\\"), it appends sourceEntry->name(), so <file source="X/Y.esp" destination=""/> installs Y.esp at the mod root.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/parse.rs:83: destination = c.attribute("destination").map(norm_path) - an explicitly empty attribute yields "" (the source fallback only applies when the attribute is absent). crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:304-312 (apply_plan): dst = dest.join("") == the mod root directory itself; fs::copy(&src, &dst) onto a directory returns EISDIR, and the error aborts the entire FOMOD install. Same for destinations ending in '/': fs::copy to "…/sub/" fails.
findings.description: destination="" on <file> entries is a very common real-world FOMOD pattern meaning 'install at Data root under the source's filename'. MO2 implements exactly that. In Eidos the copy targets the mod directory itself and the install hard-fails with an Io error for any FOMOD using this pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: In apply_plan (install.rs), for non-folder items: if item.destination is empty or ends with '/' (after the existing backslash normalization), append the final component of item.source before joining, mirroring MO2's copyLeaf.

findings.title: Context is never populated: fileDependency always evaluates as Missing and gameDependency is always true
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/installerfomod.cpp:156-206 (fileState) resolves a fileDependency name to Active/Inactive/Missing via pluginList()->state(), findFiles(), and even disabled mods; it is passed as m_FileCheck and consumed in fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:422-442 (testCondition for FileCondition). gameDependency is tested against the real game version (fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:475-519).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/engine.rs:15-23 and 31-43 implement file_states and game_version, but every call site passes Context::default(): crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:467, 516, 532, 1513, 1566 and crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:320 (apply_fomod_defaults) and 399 (finish_fomod). file_states is empty so every fileDependency reads "Missing"; game_version is None so gameDependency is unconditionally true.
findings.description: FOMODs routinely use fileDependency to auto-detect installed mods (e.g. preselect compatibility patches when an .esp is Active, mark options NotUsable when a master is missing). With an always-empty Context, state="Active"/"Inactive" conditions are always false and state="Missing" always true, so typeDescriptor patterns, step visibility, and conditionalFileInstalls give wrong results for these installers. The engine support exists; it is just never wired.
findings.suggested_fix: Build a real Context before opening the wizard / default install: populate file_states from the active profile's plugins.txt (Active/Inactive) plus the merged mods tree (anything else present = Inactive, absent = Missing), and set game_version from the detected game. Plumb it through open_fomod/finish_fomod and the GUI call sites instead of Context::default().

findings.title: <moduleDependencies> is silently discarded; MO2 aborts the install when it is unmet
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:1267-1274 (readModuleConfiguration): on <moduleDependencies> it reads the composite dependency, tests it immediately, and throws Exception(result.second) if false - the install stops with the failure message.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/parse.rs:60-72 (ModuleConfig::parse): the match on child tags handles moduleName/moduleImage/requiredInstallFiles/installSteps/conditionalFileInstalls and hits `_ => {}` for moduleDependencies - it is not even represented in model.rs ModuleConfig (model.rs:104-111).
findings.description: moduleDependencies is the FOMOD-level gate ('this mod requires SKSE 1.7+ / master X active'). Eidos installs such mods unconditionally without warning, while MO2 refuses with the dependency message. Even with finding #3 unfixed this should at least be parsed so it can be enforced once the Context is wired.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `module_dependencies: Option<Condition>` to ModuleConfig, parse it with parse_composite, and in open_fomod/apply_fomod_defaults evaluate it against the Context, returning a descriptive InstallError (or surfacing a confirm dialog) when unmet.

findings.title: order attribute ignored: MO2 defaults installSteps and plugins to Ascending (alphabetical) when order is absent
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:1125-1146 (readStepList): order defaults to ORDER_ASCENDING and pages are std::sort'ed by title (PagesAscending/Descending); fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:934-937 and 1026-1030 (readPluginList): same for plugin controls, sorted by text unless order="Explicit".
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/parse.rs:65-69 (installSteps loop) and 111-119 (parse_group/plugins) never read the order attribute; engine.rs walks steps/plugins in document order everywhere (engine.rs:104-122, 133-153).
findings.description: The FOMOD schema's default for order is Ascending, and MO2/NMM sort steps and plugins alphabetically when the attribute is omitted. Eidos always uses document order. Beyond presentation, this changes behavior: 'first usable' default picks in SelectExactlyOne/AtLeastOne groups (engine.rs:67) and step ordering, which determines which flags are visible to later steps' conditions, can differ from MO2 for FOMODs that omit order="Explicit".
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the order attribute (default Ascending) on installSteps and plugins; after parsing, sort steps by name and plugins by name for Ascending/Descending, keeping the per-file sequence counter as-is. (MO2 does not apply order to groups, so groups can stay in document order.)

findings.title: SelectExactlyOne/AtLeastOne fallback can pick a CouldBeUsable option ahead of an Optional one
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:1604-1618 (displayCurrentPage): when nothing is preselected and a selection is required, MO2 prefers first_optional, then first_couldbe (logging a warning about instability), then controls[0]. CouldBeUsable options also get a warning icon and are never preselected over an Optional (1590-1598).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fomod/src/engine.rs:67: first_usable = position of the first type != NotUsable, used as the fallback for SelectExactlyOne (engine.rs:77-81) and SelectAtLeastOne (engine.rs:85-92). A CouldBeUsable plugin listed before an Optional one wins the default selection.
findings.description: CouldBeUsable means 'may cause instability with your installed plugins'. MO2 deliberately avoids defaulting to it when an Optional alternative exists; Eidos's first-non-NotUsable fallback ignores the distinction, so a default (or non-interactive) install can pick the flagged-unstable option when a safe Optional sibling exists later in the group.
findings.suggested_fix: In default_group_selection, change the fallback chain to: first Optional, else first CouldBeUsable, else first non-NotUsable - i.e. replace first_usable with a two-tier search mirroring MO2's first_optional/first_couldbe.

findings.title: Plan sources missing from the archive are skipped with zero feedback (MO2 logs each and shows a cancellable dialog)
findings.mo2_evidence: installer_fomod/src/fomodinstallerdialog.cpp:339 and 363 (copyFileIterator) log::error each missing folder/file; updateTree (590-611) collects failures (minus the persistent ignore-list defaulting to {"no folder"}) and shows displayMissingFilesDialog (521-544) letting the user 'Install anyway' or cancel.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-install/src/install.rs:300-302 (apply_plan): `let Some(src) = resolve_ci(root, &item.source) else { continue; };` - no log, no report; InstallReport (install.rs:61-70) carries no missing-files info, so neither the CLI nor the GUI can tell the user the FOMOD referenced files the archive does not ship.
findings.description: A broken FOMOD (typo'd source path, author forgot to ship a folder) installs 'successfully' in Eidos with files silently absent - the exact failure mode MO2 warns about ('This mod may not work properly') and lets the user cancel. Silent partial installs are hard to diagnose later.
findings.suggested_fix: Collect missing FileItem sources in apply_plan, return them in InstallReport (e.g. missing: Vec<String>), log a warning per item, and have the GUI show a warning (ideally with a cancel option before finish_fomod commits). MO2's 'no folder' ignore entry can be replicated cheaply by skipping that literal source.

findings.title: Conflict relations are winner-centric; MO2 records pairwise relations among ALL providers of a file
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/modinfowithconflictinfo.cpp:176-224 - when a mod LOSES a file, the winner goes into m_OverwrittenList (l.183), and then the 'sort out the alternatives' loop (l.193-224) compares this origin against EVERY other provider pairwise: 'if (origin.getPriority() > altOrigin.getPriority()) m_OverwriteList.insert(altIndex); else m_OverwrittenList.insert(altIndex)' (l.204-207). The dataIDs re-check at l.195-196 is dead code inside this branch (the l.157 condition already excluded the only-data-alternatives case, alternatives being priority-ascending per fileentry.cpp:141-185), so all non-self mod providers are processed. Thus for one file provided by A(high)>B(mid)>C(low): B gets overwritten={A} AND overwrites={C}; C gets overwritten={A,B}.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-conflicts/src/lib.rs:120-144 - relations are derived only between the node's winner and each non-base alternative: winner.overwrites += alt (l.127-131), alt.overwritten_by += winner (l.133-143). Loser-vs-loser pairs are never recorded, so for A>B>C: B gets overwrites={} (missing C) and C gets overwritten_by={A} (missing B).
findings.description: Visible state divergence in common load orders: if mod B loses textures/x.dds to A while C also provides it, and B additionally wins any other file, MO2 shows B as CONFLICT_MIXED (overwrites C, overwritten by A) while Eidos shows plain Overwritten; C's overwritten_by set also misses B. Any file with 3+ providers (ubiquitous in real texture/body-mod setups) produces wrong emblems and wrong overwrites/overwritten_by sets. Note one trap when fixing: MO2 evaluates REDUNDANT before MIXED (modinfowithconflictinfo.cpp:229-237), so a mod that wins nothing but pairwise-overwrites a lower loser must stay Redundant; Eidos's current match arm (lib.rs:146-159) only reaches Redundant when overwrites is empty, which would wrongly yield Mixed once pairwise edges exist.
findings.suggested_fix: In ConflictMap::build's per-node loop, treat the provider list as [winner] + alternatives (already descending priority) and for every ordered pair (higher, lower) with both != BASE_ORIGIN insert higher.overwrites += lower and lower.overwritten_by += higher; also bump total for each provider as today. Then compute state with MO2's precedence: if total > 0 && won == 0 -> Redundant FIRST, then Mixed/Overwrites/Overwritten/None from the two sets. Update the fully_shadowed and mixed tests to cover a 3-provider file.

findings.title: Overwrite layer participates in the runtime mount but is absent from conflict detection (MO2 includes it at top priority)
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/profile.cpp:517-519 pins the Overwrite pseudo-mod at the highest priority (m_ModStatus.size()-1); it is alwaysEnabled (modinfooverwrite.h:38) and a ModInfoWithConflictInfo itself (modinfooverwrite.h:10), so Profile::getActiveMods (profile.cpp:602-614) feeds it into DirectoryRefresher::setMods (organizercore.cpp:1604) and it becomes an origin in the structure: mods shadowed by files in overwrite/ show CONFLICT_OVERWRITTEN, and Overwrite itself gets conflict flags.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:1296-1314 - compute_conflicts builds layers from enabled mods + game data only; the overwrite dir is never pushed. Yet at runtime the overwrite layer sits ON TOP of every mod (crates/eidos/src/main.rs:213-222 LaunchSpec { layers, overwrite, .. }; crates/eidos-core/src/lib.rs:25-42,81 'resolve_read checks the overwrite layer first').
findings.description: Eidos's Conflicts tab and mod-row emblems can disagree with what the game actually sees: a file captured into overwrite/ (e.g. a patcher output like a rebuilt mesh or generated INI fragment) silently shadows the same path in every mod, but those mods keep showing Overwrites/None. In MO2 those mods show the overwritten emblem and the user can tell why their mod's file is not taking effect - the exact scenario conflict flags exist for.
findings.suggested_fix: In compute_conflicts, push a Layer { origin: OVERWRITE_ORIGIN (a reserved non-zero id, e.g. u32::MAX), name: "Overwrite".into(), root: inst.overwrite_dir() } at the FRONT of the layer vec (highest priority), treating it as a normal mod origin (not BASE_ORIGIN) so shadowed mods get overwritten_by entries. Skip whiteout marker files (WHITEOUT_PREFIX names from eidos-core) when walking that layer. Optionally show the Overwrite pseudo-row's own state in conflicts_panel like MO2 does.

findings.title: hasHiddenFiles is computed and surfaced by MO2's conflict check but dropped entirely by Eidos
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/modinfowithconflictinfo.cpp:100,123-153 - doConflictCheck sets hasHiddenFiles when any file (or any parent directory) ends with .mohidden, stores it in the Conflicts struct (l.255), and getFlags() (l.37-44) surfaces FLAG_HIDDEN_FILES in the mod list flags column, so a mod whose content is partly/fully hidden is visibly flagged (state itself stays CONFLICT_NONE for an all-hidden mod, which Eidos matches).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-conflicts/src/lib.rs:186-189 - collect_files silently skips *.mohidden entries; ModConflicts (l.71-82) has no hidden-files field and the GUI flags cell (crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:1036-1051) only renders the four conflict emblems. grep over the workspace shows no other .mohidden tracking.
findings.description: The conflict-state outcome matches MO2 (an all-hidden mod is None, not Redundant), but the information that a mod has hidden files is lost. In MO2 this flag is the only cue that a mod which 'does nothing' was deliberately neutered via Hide-file actions; without it an Eidos user sees a completely unflagged mod and has no hint why its files are inert.
findings.suggested_fix: Have collect_files (or a small wrapper) also return a has_hidden: bool per layer (set when a *.mohidden file or directory is skipped), store it on ModConflicts (e.g. pub has_hidden: bool), and render a hidden-files glyph in the mod-row flags cell alongside the conflict emblem, mirroring MO2's separate FLAG_HIDDEN_FILES.

findings.title: BSA invalidation incomplete for pre-SSE games (Oblivion/FO3/FNV): missing dummy BSA + SArchiveList + SInvalidationFile dance
findings.mo2_evidence: game_gamebryo/src/gamebryo/gamebryobsainvalidation.cpp:43-99 - prepareProfile() writes bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 AND (when invalidation is active) registers the invalidation BSA at index 0 of the archive list via m_DataArchives->addArchive(profile, 0, invalidationBSAName()) (line 76), creates the dummy BSA file in the game Data dir via DummyBSA::write (lines 81-86, writer in game_gamebryo/src/gamebryo/dummybsa.cpp), and sets SInvalidationFile="" (lines 89-99). gamebryodataarchives.cpp:57 implements the SArchiveList edit.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-gamefeatures/src/lib.rs:31-33 - enable_bsa_invalidation() only writes [Archive] bInvalidateOlderFiles=1; the module doc at lines 8-9 even acknowledges MO2 does 'a dummy BSA + SInvalidationFile dance for pre-SSE engines' but it is not implemented. Eidos applies this single key to every supported game, and eidos-gamedef/src/lib.rs declares pre-SSE games: oblivion (line 202), fallout3 (line 186), falloutnv (line 170), skyrim LE (line 112). Called per-launch from crates/eidos/src/main.rs:92-97.
findings.description: On Oblivion, Fallout 3 and Fallout NV (all games Eidos detects and manages), bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 alone is not sufficient for loose mod files to override assets packed in the vanilla BSAs - that is exactly why MO2's GamebryoBSAInvalidation creates a dummy invalidation BSA, prepends it to SArchiveList, and blanks SInvalidationFile. With Eidos's current implementation, texture/mesh replacers for BSA'd assets on these engines silently do not appear in-game - the worst failure class for a mod manager, with no error anywhere. (SSE/FO4/Starfield are fine with the single key.)
findings.suggested_fix: Port the full GamebryoBSAInvalidation behavior for pre-SSE game ids: write a minimal dummy BSA (port dummybsa.cpp; version differs per engine) into the mount's overwrite/Data layer or game Data dir, prepend its name to SArchiveList in the deployed INI (Eidos already has format-preserving eidos_ini::set_key), and set SInvalidationFile=. Gate it on game id so SSE-era games keep the current single-key path.

findings.title: modlist.txt is overwritten in place (fs::write) - a crash/ENOSPC mid-write destroys the profile's mod order; MO2 writes atomically via QSaveFile
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/profile.cpp:243-281 - doWriteModlist() writes through SafeWriteFile and only file->commit() (line 276) atomically replaces modlist.txt; uibase/src/safewritefile.cpp:28-48 wraps QSaveFile (temp file + atomic commit, with disk-space error reporting). MO2 additionally surfaces orphaned QSaveFile temporaries in the restore dialog (modorganizer/src/mainwindow.cpp:3862-3878) and keeps up to 10 timestamped modlist.txt.<date> backups (mainwindow.cpp:3828-3839, 3918-3925).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/profile.rs:225-234 - save_modlist() builds the string then `fs::write(self.modlist_path(), s)`, which truncates the existing file before writing. Called on every toggle/move from the GUI (crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:312) and CLI (crates/eidos/src/main.rs:408).
findings.description: fs::write opens with O_TRUNC, so the old modlist is destroyed before the new bytes land. A crash, power loss, or full disk between truncate and write leaves an empty/partial modlist.txt; Eidos's reconcile logic then silently rebuilds it as 'every mod enabled, alphabetical order', losing the user's entire curated order and disabled set with no recovery path. MO2 treats this file as precious: atomic QSaveFile commit plus user-restorable backups. Since save_modlist runs on every single checkbox click, the write frequency makes the window non-theoretical.
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a temp file in the same profile directory (e.g. modlist.txt.tmp) and fs::rename() over modlist.txt (atomic on the same filesystem). Optionally keep a one-deep modlist.txt.bak of the previous contents before the rename, mirroring MO2's backup affordance cheaply.

findings.title: Profile rename/delete leave manifest.selected_profile dangling; a ghost active profile silently launches with ALL mods enabled
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/profilesdialog.cpp:235-240 refuses to delete the active profile and 287-292 refuses to rename it ('Please change to a different profile first'). As a second line of defense, modorganizer/src/organizercore.cpp:578-594 validates the selected profile at switch/startup (case-insensitive directory walk, lines 563-576), and if it does not exist creates a default profile, picks an existing one, and shows the user an error.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/profile.rs:171-179 - rename() and delete() mutate the directory with no active-profile guard and never touch the manifest; crates/eidos-instance/src/lib.rs:194-198 - active_profile() returns manifest.selected_profile verbatim with no existence check, and lib.rs:210-212 active() builds a Profile from it. For a nonexistent profile, modlist() (profile.rs:198-221) finds no modlist.txt and falls through to 'append every present mod, enabled=true' (profile.rs:216-220), and save_modlist (profile.rs:226) recreates the deleted directory.
findings.description: rename()/delete() are public library API (the GUI has no rename/delete UI yet, but the functions are implemented and any caller - future GUI wiring, CLI, or a hand-edited/copied manifest - hits this). Once selected_profile names a gone directory, `eidos play` silently mounts every installed mod in alphabetical order instead of the user's profile, and the first GUI save resurrects the dead profile as a ghost with that wrong state. MO2 makes this state unreachable (guards) and self-healing with a visible warning (fallback).
findings.suggested_fix: In Profile::rename(), validate the new name (reject empty / path separators / '..', like MO2's fixDirectoryName) and have the caller update manifest.selected_profile when the renamed profile is active (or do it in an Instance::rename_profile wrapper). In Profile::delete()/Instance, either refuse to delete the active profile or reset selected_profile to an existing one. In active_profile(), verify profiles/<name> exists and fall back to the first existing profile (or Default) with a logged warning instead of returning the dangling name.

findings.title: create_from skips the saves/ subdirectory - MO2's profile copy is fully recursive, and the Eidos copy later seeds saves from the stale prefix instead
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/profile.cpp:729-740 - createPtrFrom() calls reference.copyFilesTo(target) which is copyDir(m_Directory.absolutePath(), target, false); uibase/src/utility.cpp:82-112 - copyDir copies all files AND recurses into every subdirectory (lines 104-110), so a copied profile gets the reference profile's saves/ (and settings.ini) along with modlist/plugins/INIs.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/profile.rs:159-169 - create_from() copies only entries where e.path().is_file(), with the doc comment 'Subdirectories (saves) are not copied.' Interaction: on the copied profile's first launch, seed_saves (profile.rs:118-136, called from crates/eidos/src/main.rs:115) sees an empty saves_dir and seeds it from the prefix's Saves dir - which, under Eidos's bind-mount model, still holds the stale pre-Eidos saves, not the source profile's playthrough.
findings.description: In MO2, duplicating a profile clones the playthrough: local saves come along, so 'copy profile to test something' continues exactly where the source profile was. In Eidos the copy starts saveless, and the seed-on-launch logic then quietly fills it with whatever was in the Proton prefix before Eidos adopted it - typically an old, unrelated save set. The user sees a copied profile whose saves are neither empty nor the source profile's: a confusing playthrough mixup that MO2's recursive copy avoids by construction.
findings.suggested_fix: In create_from(), also copy the source profile's saves/ subdirectory recursively (a simple walk; symlink-skipping like MO2's copyDir). If not copying saves is intended as a deliberate divergence, at least create an empty saves/ dir in the new profile so seed_saves does not adopt the stale prefix saves into it.

findings.title: Modlist parser mishandles MO2's '*' (unmanaged/foreign) lines and does not trim the name after the +/- marker
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/profile.cpp:455-462 - refreshModStatus() treats a leading '*' like '+' (enabled, foreign) and parses the name as line.mid(1).trimmed() (whitespace after the marker is stripped); doWriteModlist writes '*' lines for foreign mods (profile.cpp:264-265), so real MO2 modlist.txt files contain them (e.g. '*DLC: Dawnguard').
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/profile.rs:204-210 - modlist() only strips '+' and '-'; any other line, including '*Name', falls into the else branch and is treated as a mod literally named '*Name' (enabled). Since no mods/ directory matches that name it is dropped from the view (profile.rs:211) and permanently erased by the next save_modlist (profile.rs:225-234). The prefix is stripped without a subsequent trim, so '+ Name' yields the name ' Name'.
findings.description: The file format is documented as 'MO2 style' (profile.rs:5-7, lib.rs:12) and Eidos otherwise aims at MO2 interop (MO2-compatible meta.ini, MO2-format download .meta). A user who points Eidos at a modlist.txt carried over from MO2 - the obvious migration move - silently loses every '*' line on first save, and hand-edited lines with whitespace after the marker fail to match their mod directory. Eidos's own writes are unaffected, hence low severity.
findings.suggested_fix: In the parser, treat a leading '*' like '+' (one extra strip_prefix arm) and trim the name after removing the marker, matching MO2's mid(1).trimmed(). Optionally preserve unmatched '*' lines on save instead of dropping them, since Eidos does not model foreign mods yet.

findings.title: Fallout 4 / Starfield invalidation missing sResourceDataDirsFinal= (FO4 also written to wrong INI)
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer-game_fallout4/src/fallout4bsainvalidation.cpp:33-66 (fetched from ModOrganizer2 master, local copy /tmp/mo2games/game_fallout4/): Fallout4BSAInvalidation::prepareProfile writes BOTH [Archive] bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 AND sResourceDataDirsFinal="" into Fallout4Custom.ini (constructor lines 12-15 hardcode "Fallout4Custom.ini"); registered in gamefallout4.cpp:51. modorganizer-game_starfield/src/starfieldbsainvalidation.cpp:33-66 is identical for StarfieldCustom.ini (registered gamestarfield.cpp:54).
findings.eidos_evidence: /home/mothersphere/Documents/Repositories/Eidos/crates/eidos-gamefeatures/src/lib.rs:31-33: enable_bsa_invalidation writes ONLY bInvalidateOlderFiles=1; called from crates/eidos/src/main.rs:92-96 with ini_files[0], which for fallout4/fallout4vr is "Fallout4.ini" (crates/eidos-gamedef/src/lib.rs:148,164), for starfield "StarfieldCustom.ini" (lib.rs:238). No sResourceDataDirsFinal anywhere in the repo (grep confirms).
findings.description: FO4 and Starfield ship with sResourceDataDirsFinal=STRINGS\, meaning the engine only scans Data/Strings for loose files. bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 alone does nothing for textures/meshes/interface/scripts - loose-file mods are silently ignored, which defeats the entire point of the feature. MO2 clears the key to "" alongside setting bInvalidateOlderFiles. Additionally MO2 puts both keys in Fallout4Custom.ini (which overrides Fallout4.ini), so a user's pre-existing Fallout4Custom.ini carrying the vanilla defaults can override Eidos's write to Fallout4.ini even if Eidos added the second key there.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the invalidation write data-driven per game: add to GameDef an invalidation INI target + key list (fallout4/fallout4vr -> Fallout4Custom.ini, starfield -> StarfieldCustom.ini, with both bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 and sResourceDataDirsFinal=). enable_bsa_invalidation then iterates the keys via the existing set_ini_key. Requires adding Fallout4Custom.ini to the FO4 ini_files set (see separate finding).

findings.title: Oblivion/FNV/FO3 invalidation incomplete: dummy BSA + SArchiveList registration + SInvalidationFile="" missing
findings.mo2_evidence: mo2-study/game_gamebryo/src/gamebryo/gamebryobsainvalidation.cpp:64-99: when invalidation is active MO2 (a) inserts the invalidation BSA at index 0 of the INI archive list (m_DataArchives->addArchive(profile, 0, ...), line 76), (b) writes the dummy BSA into the game's Data dir (lines 81-86, format in gamebryo/dummybsa.cpp:106-192), (c) sets [Archive] SInvalidationFile="" (lines 88-99). Per-game: oblivionbsainvalidation.cpp ("Oblivion - Invalidation.bsa", version 0x67, SArchiveList in oblivion.ini per obliviondataarchives.cpp:11-32), falloutnvbsainvalidation.cpp / fallout3bsainvalidation ("Fallout - Invalidation.bsa", 0x68, SArchiveList in fallout.ini), skyrimbsainvalidation.cpp ("Skyrim - Invalidation.bsa", sResourceArchiveList in skyrim.ini).
findings.eidos_evidence: /home/mothersphere/Documents/Repositories/Eidos/crates/eidos-gamefeatures/src/lib.rs:31-33 writes only bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 for every game; the doc comment at lib.rs:8-9 even names the "dummy BSA + SInvalidationFile dance for pre-SSE engines" but it is not implemented. crates/eidos/src/main.rs:91-97 is the only call site. No SArchiveList/SInvalidationFile/dummy-BSA code exists in any crate (grep confirms).
findings.description: On the pre-SSE engines (Oblivion, FO3, FNV; Skyrim LE gets the same treatment in MO2) bInvalidateOlderFiles=1 is timestamp-relative: a loose file only overrides BSA content if its mtime is newer than the owning archive. Mod files extracted with preserved archive timestamps are routinely older than the Steam-installed BSAs, so overrides fail intermittently and silently - exactly the failure mode the dummy-BSA method ("ArchiveInvalidation Invalidated") exists to fix. MO2 also resets SInvalidationFile to empty so the legacy ArchiveInvalidation.txt mechanism does not interfere. Eidos claims these games as supported, so this is a correctness gap, not roadmap.
findings.suggested_fix: Port dummybsa.cpp (~190 lines, trivial in Rust) and write the per-game invalidation BSA. To respect Eidos's no-game-dir-mutation principle, place it in an internal always-on overlay layer instead of the real Data dir. Add archive-list INI management (SArchiveList for Oblivion/FO3/FNV with comma-join, the 255-char sResourceArchiveList/List2 split for Skyrim LE per skyrimdataarchives.cpp:27-41) and insert the invalidation BSA at index 0; set SInvalidationFile= in the same profile INI Eidos already deploys.

findings.title: Per-profile INI sets missing the Custom INIs MO2 manages (Fallout4Custom.ini, SkyrimCustom.ini, FalloutCustom.ini, OblivionPrefs.ini)
findings.mo2_evidence: iniFiles() per MO2 game plugin (fetched masters, /tmp/mo2games/): gamefallout4.cpp:230 {fallout4.ini, fallout4prefs.ini, fallout4custom.ini} (initializeProfile copies all three); gamefallout4vr.cpp:176-179 {fallout4.ini, fallout4custom.ini, fallout4prefs.ini}; gameskyrimse.cpp:281-284 {skyrim.ini, skyrimprefs.ini, skyrimcustom.ini}; gamefalloutnv.cpp:283-287 and gamefallout3.cpp:247-251 add falloutcustom.ini + GECKCustom.ini + GECKPrefs.ini; gameoblivion.cpp:171-174 {oblivion.ini, oblivionprefs.ini}.
findings.eidos_evidence: /home/mothersphere/Documents/Repositories/Eidos/crates/eidos-gamedef/src/lib.rs: skyrimse:90 and fallout4:148 list only base+prefs; fallout4vr:164 same; falloutnv:177 and fallout3:193 only Fallout.ini+FalloutPrefs.ini; oblivion:209 only Oblivion.ini. These feed seed/deploy/capture in crates/eidos-instance/src/profile.rs:60-116 via crates/eidos/src/main.rs:74-90,227-229.
findings.description: Eidos's per-profile INI seed/deploy/capture cycle only covers the files listed in ini_files, so the Custom INIs - where modding guides, ENB setups, and mods put most user settings on SSE/FO4, and where FO4's invalidation must live - leak across profiles: they are not snapshotted per profile, not restored on deploy, and in-game changes to them are never captured. MO2 treats them as first-class profile INIs. (Starfield already matches: StarfieldCustom.ini+StarfieldPrefs.ini.) GECK INIs are optional polish; FalloutCustom/SkyrimCustom/Fallout4Custom/OblivionPrefs are the consequential ones.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the ini_files rows: skyrimse += SkyrimCustom.ini; fallout4/fallout4vr += Fallout4Custom.ini; falloutnv/fallout3 += FalloutCustom.ini (and optionally the GECK pair); oblivion += OblivionPrefs.ini. Keep the [Archive]-carrying file first per the existing convention. seed_inis already tolerates missing source files, so no other code changes needed.

findings.title: Morrowind has zero INI/archive support though MO2 manages morrowind.ini including invalidation and the [Archives] list
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer-game_morrowind (fetched master, /tmp/mo2games/game_morrowind/): gamemorrowind.cpp:183-186 iniFiles {"morrowind.ini"}; gamemorrowind.cpp:43-45 registers MorrowindDataArchives + MorrowindBSAInvalidation; morrowinddataarchives.cpp:48-75 reads/writes [Archives] "Archive 0..N" keys in morrowind.ini located in the GAME directory (gameDirectory(), not My Games); morrowindbsainvalidation.cpp uses "Morrowind - Invalidation.bsa".
findings.eidos_evidence: /home/mothersphere/Documents/Repositories/Eidos/crates/eidos-gamedef/src/lib.rs:224-225: morrowind row has documents_dir: "" and ini_files: &[], so crates/eidos/src/main.rs:74-77 returns None and skips ALL INI handling - no per-profile INI, no invalidation, no archive registration.
findings.description: Morrowind keeps morrowind.ini in the install dir, which Eidos's Documents-anchored INI machinery cannot express, so the game silently gets no INI features at all. Two consequences within claimed support: (1) mod BSAs can only load if registered as [Archives] Archive N= entries in morrowind.ini - MO2 manages that list; Eidos cannot, so BSA-shipping Morrowind mods never load; (2) MO2 also applies the dummy-BSA invalidation to Morrowind. Morrowind plugin load-order is already documented as unmanaged, but the INI side is this subsystem's gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Teach the INI feature layer a per-game INI base location (documents vs game dir): for Morrowind point seed/deploy/capture and future archive-list management at <install>/Morrowind.ini. Then implement the [Archives] Archive N= list read/write (per morrowinddataarchives.cpp:13-46, including the rewrite-whole-section approach) so mod BSAs and the invalidation BSA can be registered.

findings.title: MO2 writes [Launcher] bEnableFileSelection=1 before every run; Eidos never does
