findings.title: CDN-derived download filename is not sanitized: encoded '../' escapes the downloads dir
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/downloadmanager.cpp:537,600,616 and getDownloadFileName at 1613-1626 pass every candidate name through MOBase::sanitizeFileName before composing the output path; uibase/src/filesystemutilities.cpp:37-54 strips \\ / : * ? " < > | and control chars and forbids '.'/'..'. MO2 also derives the name via QFileInfo(URL).fileName() BEFORE any decoding.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:239-262 file_name_from_uri() splits the raw URI on '/' first, then percent-decodes the last segment, so '%2F' and '%2E%2E%2F' decode INTO the returned name; crates/eidos/src/main.rs:638-641 joins that name into inst.downloads_dir() unmodified, and lib.rs:212-214 download() does fs::create_dir_all(dest.parent()) then writes there.
findings.description: A download_link API response whose URI ends in e.g. '.../%2e%2e%2fevil.7z' yields the name '../evil.7z'; dest becomes downloads/../evil.7z, so the archive (and its .meta via write_download_meta) are written into the instance root (next to mods/, overwrite/, load_order.txt) or higher with more '..' segments. file.file_name from the files/{id} endpoint is joined the same way (main.rs:639). MO2 treats all of these as untrusted and sanitizes; Eidos trusts the API/CDN response verbatim. Defense-in-depth bug rather than a remote exploit (the data comes from Nexus over TLS), but it also silently creates subdirectories for any benign '%2F' in a name.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize the decoded name before joining: replace '/' and '\\' (and control chars) with '_', strip trailing dots/spaces, reject '.', '..' and empty results (fall back to the existing '<modid>-<fileid>.archive' name). Mirror MOBase::sanitizeFileName in eidos-nexus and apply it to both file_name_from_uri() results and RemoteFile::file_name.

findings.title: cmd_nxm silently overwrites an existing archive of the same name (MO2 prompts and uniquifies)
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/downloadmanager.cpp:599-616: if the file already exists in the downloads dir, MO2 asks 'Download again? The new file will receive a different name' and on yes renames via getDownloadFileName(baseName, true) which picks '<i>_<name>' (1613-1626). It also dedups by mod/file id against pending (786-802) and active (804-851) downloads, returning the existing download's id.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos/src/main.rs:641 'let dest = inst.downloads_dir().join(&name);' with no existence check; crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:215-220 download() does fs::File::create(tmp) (truncates any leftover) then fs::rename(tmp, dest), which on Linux silently replaces an existing dest; write_download_meta (lib.rs:268-297) then rewrites the .meta from scratch.
findings.description: Re-clicking 'Mod Manager Download' (or re-running 'eidos nxm') for a file that is already on disk re-downloads and clobbers both the archive and its .meta sidecar with no warning. Besides wasting bandwidth/quota, it destroys any sidecar state and, in the rare case where two different Nexus files share an archive name, destroys the other file's download entirely. MO2 never silently overwrites a completed download.
findings.suggested_fix: Before downloading, stat dest: if it exists and its .meta matches this modID/fileID, print 'already downloaded: <path>' and exit 0 (CLI equivalent of MO2's 'No' answer); otherwise uniquify the name with MO2's '<i>_<name>' scheme before downloading.

findings.title: Update check can never report updates published more than one month ago
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/modinfo.cpp:299-387 checkAllForUpdate(): MO2 tracks per-mod lastNexusUpdate; if any mod hasn't been checked within a month (337-363) it queries those mods INDIVIDUALLY (requestUpdates per mod) before trusting the bulk endpoint, and otherwise picks the period (1d/1w/1m) from the EARLIEST last check (364-384). The 1m bulk list is only valid for mods already checked within that window.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos/src/main.rs:513-547 cmd_nexus update: unconditionally fetches mods/updated?period=1m (515) and then skips every installed mod whose id is not in that set (528-530). No lastNexusUpdate tracking exists; mods outside the window are never queried, in this run or any future run.
findings.description: games/{game}/mods/updated?period=1m only lists mods whose latest change is within the last month. If the user installs an old version of a mod whose last Nexus update was 2+ months ago, Eidos's check skips it forever and the summary prints '0 update(s) available' - the feature silently returns wrong results in the most common first-run scenario (an established mod list). MO2 explicitly engineered around this exact hole.
findings.suggested_fix: Record lastNexusUpdate (timestamp) in each mod's meta.ini when it is checked. On 'eidos nexus update', mods with a missing or >1-month-old lastNexusUpdate get an individual mod_info query regardless of the bulk intersection (with a note about extra API requests, like MO2's log message); only mods checked within the window may rely on the updated?period=1m intersection.

findings.title: Interrupted downloads cannot resume: no HTTP Range support, partial file is discarded
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/downloadmanager.cpp:1047-1098 resumeDownloadInt(): sets m_ResumePos = output.size(), sends 'Range: bytes=<pos>-' (1086-1088) and reopens the output with QIODevice::Append (680-683), so a dropped connection or restart continues where it left off. Partials persist as '<name>.unfinished' and are picked up again.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:210-222 download(): fs::File::create(&tmp) truncates any existing partial and the GET has no Range header; an interrupted 'eidos nxm' leaves the .unfinished behind and the next attempt restarts from byte 0.
findings.description: Within the already-implemented download path, a network drop or Ctrl-C on a multi-GB archive (common for Skyrim texture packs) throws away everything received. MO2 Range-resumes the .unfinished file. For free Nexus accounts with capped download speed this is a substantial practical regression; it also burns a fresh download_link request (and for non-premium users the one-shot key may have expired, forcing a trip back to the browser).
findings.suggested_fix: In Nexus::download(), if '<dest>.unfinished' exists, open it in append mode, send 'Range: bytes=<len>-', and only restart from scratch when the server answers 200 instead of 206 (then truncate). Keep the final rename-on-complete as is.

findings.title: Rate-limit headers (X-RL-*) are ignored and the update loop keeps firing requests after a 429
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/nexusinterface.cpp:250-270 parseLimits() reads x-rl-daily-limit/-remaining and x-rl-hourly-limit/-remaining; 1180 updates m_User.limits on EVERY successful reply; 1064-1075 re-parses them on a 429; 869-883 nextRequest() halts and clears the whole queue when m_User.exhausted(), telling the user when the next batch is available. Defaults are 2500/day and only 100/hour (229-243).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:125-140 Nexus::get() discards all response headers and maps 429 to a plain error string; crates/eidos/src/main.rs:524-547 the cmd_nexus update loop catches each mod_info error with 'eprintln' and CONTINUES iterating, issuing one more doomed request per remaining mod.
findings.description: With a large mod list (>100 mods in the 1m intersection - the hourly cap is 100), Eidos exhausts the hourly budget mid-loop, then spams a 429'd request for every remaining mod, and never tells the user how much quota is left or when to retry. MO2 stops dispatching the moment the account is exhausted and surfaces remaining requests in the UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Have Nexus::get() capture X-RL-Hourly-Remaining/X-RL-Daily-Remaining into the client (ureq exposes resp.header()). In cmd_nexus update: abort the loop on the first 429 with a 'rate limited, N mods unchecked, retry after the hour' message, and print the remaining hourly/daily budget in the final summary line.

findings.title: .unfinished marker replaces the archive extension instead of appending
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/downloadmanager.cpp:57 'static const char UNFINISHED[] = ".unfinished";' is appended to the full file name (e.g. 1340: 'const auto unfinished = path + ".unfinished"'; 2460-2475 completion just strips the suffix), so the partial is 'Mod-1.0.7z.unfinished' and the real name survives.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:215 'let tmp = dest.with_extension("unfinished");' - Path::with_extension REPLACES the last extension, producing 'Mod-1.0.unfinished' for 'Mod-1.0.7z'. Contrast with Eidos's own sidecar convention which correctly appends (lib.rs:276 format!("{}.meta", ...) and eidos-install/src/install.rs:192-193 'the full archive name + ".meta"').
findings.description: The comment on lib.rs:215 claims this is 'MO2's in-progress marker' but the produced name is not MO2's format: the real archive extension is destroyed, so a leftover partial can no longer be mapped back to its destination (blocking the Range-resume fix), and two files differing only by extension ('Foo.7z' vs 'Foo.zip') collide on the same 'Foo.unfinished' temp name.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the temp path by appending: 'let tmp = PathBuf::from(format!("{}.unfinished", dest.display()));' - one line, and it matches both MO2 and Eidos's .meta convention.

findings.title: API requests omit Protocol-Version / Application-Name / Application-Version headers
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/nxmaccessmanager.cpp:994-1006 addAPIHeaders() sets User-Agent, Content-Type: application/json, 'Protocol-Version: 1.0.0', 'Application-Name: MO2', 'Application-Version: <MO version>' on every v1 API request (applied in nexusinterface.cpp:1018-1019 alongside APIKEY); userAgent() (1087-1105) is 'Mod Organizer/<ver> (<OS>; <arch>) Qt/<qt>'.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:118-131: the ureq agent sends only 'User-Agent: Eidos/<ver> (Linux)' plus the APIKEY header; no Protocol-Version, Application-Name, or Application-Version.
findings.description: The Nexus public API asks clients to identify themselves via Application-Name/Application-Version (this is how Nexus attributes traffic and contacts authors of misbehaving apps; MO2 sends all three headers on every call). Eidos's User-Agent does carry app/version/OS, so this is compliance polish rather than a functional break, but it is a literal 5-line parity gap in the exact code Eidos's module doc claims to mirror.
findings.suggested_fix: In Nexus::get(), add .set("Protocol-Version", "1.0.0"), .set("Application-Name", "Eidos"), .set("Application-Version", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")); optionally enrich the User-Agent with kernel/arch ('Eidos/<ver> (Linux <arch>)').

findings.title: .meta lifecycle flags are written once and never maintained (installed stays false forever)
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/downloadmanager.cpp:1540-1572 markInstalled() flips installed=true/uninstalled=false in the sidecar when the archive is installed; 1579-1611 markUninstalled(); 1794-1798 createMetaFile keeps installed/uninstalled/paused/removed in sync with download state; 101-122 the list reader uses these flags to restore STATE_INSTALLED/UNINSTALLED/PAUSED and hide removed entries.
findings.eidos_evidence:
crates/eidos-nexus/src/lib.rs:294 writes the literal block 'installed=false
uninstalled=false
paused=false
removed=false' at download time; no other code in the repo ever updates the sidecar - eidos-install/src/install.rs:191-216 only READS it to seed meta.ini, and the GUI Downloads tab (crates/eidos-gui/src/main.rs:1171-1177) reads only the version.
findings.description: Eidos chose to emit MO2's lifecycle keys but treats them as constants, so after 'eidos install' the sidecar still claims installed=false. Consequences today: the Downloads tab cannot distinguish already-installed archives (MO2 greys/sorts them) and a downloads folder shared or migrated to MO2 shows every Eidos-installed archive as never-installed. The data model is already there; only the flip is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: After a successful install_archive() from a downloads/ archive (CLI cmd_install and the GUI Install button), rewrite the sidecar with installed=true, uninstalled=false (a tiny mark_installed(archive: &Path) helper in eidos-nexus or eidos-instance). Use it in the Downloads tab to badge installed entries.

findings.title: Plugins created in the Overwrite layer are dropped from plugins.txt on the next run
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/modinfo.cpp:114,272 (Overwrite registered as an always-present pseudo-mod via createFromOverwrite), organizercore.cpp:1600-1605 (refreshDirectoryStructure feeds getActiveMods - which includes Overwrite at top priority - into the DirectoryRefresher), pluginlist.cpp:237-301 (PluginList::refresh enumerates the merged structure, so Overwrite-origin ESPs enter the plugin list), organizercore.cpp:2134-2143 (overwrite dir also mapped into the VFS). Net effect: a plugin that exists only in Overwrite (xEdit output, 'Bashed Patch, 0.esp', generated patches) is listed and written to plugins.txt by savePluginList in afterRun.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos/src/main.rs:36-40 - prepare_plugins builds sources as the game Data dir plus enabled mods only; inst.overwrite_dir() is never added, even though crates/eidos-launch/src/lib.rs:130 mounts it as the writable top layer (Eidos::new(layers, spec.overwrite)) so such plugins ARE visible to the game through the union. crates/eidos-plugins/src/loadorder.rs:108-121 apply_active maps the prefix plugins.txt onto discovered plugins only, and write_load_order (loadorder.rs:42-78) rewrites plugins.txt from that list.
findings.description: Run xEdit or Wrye Bash through 'eidos tool': any new .esp/.esm it creates goes to the copy-on-write Overwrite layer. The tool activates it in the prefix plugins.txt. On the NEXT eidos run, prepare_plugins re-discovers plugins from Data + mods, never sees the Overwrite-only plugin, apply_active silently ignores its plugins.txt line (no matching discovered plugin), and write_load_order rewrites plugins.txt without it. The game stops loading the generated patch with no warning - the classic Bashed Patch workflow breaks one run after it works. Secondary: header parsing (main.rs:42 discover) also reads masters from the mod-source copy even when a cleaned copy in Overwrite shadows it.
findings.suggested_fix: In prepare_plugins, append ("overwrite", inst.overwrite_dir()) as the last (highest-priority) source so Overwrite plugins are discovered and win same-name shadowing, mirroring MO2's always-active top-priority Overwrite mod. Prefer the Overwrite copy for header parsing when it shadows a mod plugin.

findings.title: Tool launches via 'proton run' never set SteamAppId/SteamGameId
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/spawn.cpp:616-622 - checkSteam() sets env SteamAPPId to the per-executable steamAppID (Executable::steamAppID(), processrunner.cpp:471-475,568,640-654) or the global setting before every spawn; processrunner.cpp:783 calls checkSteam on every runBinary, so all children inherit the app id.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-games/src/proton.rs:163-175 - ProtonRun.env contains only STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH and STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH; crates/eidos/src/main.rs:353-378 passes run.env unchanged into run_through_view -> LaunchSpec.env (eidos-launch/src/lib.rs:141). No SteamAppId/SteamGameId/STEAM_COMPAT_APP_ID anywhere ('eidos play' is fine because Steam's %command% environment is inherited; 'eidos tool' is not).
findings.description: MO2 guarantees every launched executable sees the game's Steam app id. Eidos tool runs launch Proton protontricks-style with only the two COMPAT vars: steam_api.dll-using tools fail to initialize (no steam_appid.txt and no SteamAppId env), GE-Proton's protonfixes can't identify the game so per-game fixes are skipped, and Proton log naming/overlay behavior keyed on SteamGameId degrades. game.def.steam_app_id is already in scope at the call site (main.rs:353).
findings.suggested_fix: In proton_command() (or cmd_tool before run_through_view), add ("SteamAppId", app_id), ("SteamGameId", app_id) and ("STEAM_COMPAT_APP_ID", app_id) to ProtonRun.env, matching MO2's per-executable steamAppID with the game's app id as default.

findings.title: Union is unmounted when the direct child exits, not when the process tree is done
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/processrunner.cpp:355-401 - waitForProcesses creates a job object ('using a job so any child process started by any of those processes can also be captured and monitored'), assigns the spawned process, and waitForProcessesThreadImpl (284-342) keeps waiting while ANY interesting descendant lives; afterRun/teardown only happens after the whole tree exits.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-launch/src/lib.rs:152-155 - 'let status = cmd.status(); drop(session); status': the FUSE BackgroundSession (a thread inside the eidos process, eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:227-229 fuser::spawn_mount2) is dropped, unmounting, the instant the DIRECT child exits.
findings.description: Proton's 'run' verb waits only for its immediate wine process. A tool that spawns a sibling Windows process and exits (Wrye Bash launching the game, a loader-style tool, FNIS spawning a worker) leaves grandchildren running when cmd.status() returns; Eidos then unmounts the union and exits, killing the FUSE daemon, and the surviving process gets ENOTCONN/empty Data mid-run. capture_inis also runs before the real workload has exited. The game path under Steam is protected only incidentally by Steam's reaper (its subreaper waits for all descendants); 'eidos tool' has no such shield.
findings.suggested_fix: Before spawning, prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1) in the namespace process; after the direct child exits, loop waitpid(-1, ...) until ECHILD (i.e. all reparented descendants are gone) before dropping the FUSE session and capturing INIs - the Linux equivalent of MO2's job-object wait.

findings.title: PlainList games: disabled plugins are resurrected and inactive order lost (loadorder.txt written but never read)
findings.mo2_evidence: game_gamebryo/src/gamebryo/gamebryogameplugins.cpp:38-58 - readPluginLists reads loadorder.txt for the FULL order and plugins.txt for active state; 236-244 - plugins NOT listed in plugins.txt are explicitly setState(STATE_INACTIVE). Both files round-trip the user's state for Skyrim LE/FO3/FNV.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-plugins/src/loadorder.rs:83-102 - read_active reads ONLY plugins.txt and for PlainList marks every listed plugin active; loadorder.rs:108-121 - apply_active leaves plugins absent from the list at their discover() default enabled=true and sorts them to the end (usize::MAX); loadorder.txt is written (loadorder.rs:71-76) but no code path ever reads it. Used by crates/eidos/src/main.rs:44-49.
findings.description: For Asterisk games the round trip works (disabled = unstarred line). For PlainList games (skyrim, fallout3, falloutnv - all supported per eidos-plugins/src/lib.rs:78-85) a disabled plugin is simply absent from plugins.txt, so the only persisted signal of 'disabled' is its presence in loadorder.txt without a plugins.txt line. Eidos ignores loadorder.txt, so on every run all previously deactivated plugins come back enabled (including a migrated MO2 FNV setup's deliberately inactive plugins, and plugins a tool like Wrye Bash deactivated before building a patch), and inactive plugins lose their load-order slot.
findings.suggested_fix: For PlainList specs, have read_active also parse loadorder.txt: use it for ordering, and mark plugins present in loadorder.txt but absent from plugins.txt as enabled=false (absent from both = genuinely new, keep default enabled) - mirroring gamebryogameplugins.cpp readPluginLists.

findings.title: Forced-libraries support (wine_dll_overrides) is implemented but never wired into any launch
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/organizercore.cpp:2027-2028 - beforeRun calls m_USVFS.updateForcedLibraries(forcedLibraries) on EVERY run; processrunner.cpp:555-558 and 643-645 resolve the per-executable forced-library list (profile->determineForcedLibraries) and pass it down, so mod-provided ENB/ReShade/.asi loader DLLs are force-loaded.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-launch/src/lib.rs:158-171 - wine_dll_overrides() exists, is tested (173-191), and LaunchSpec.env's doc (lib.rs:28-30) names WINEDLLOVERRIDES as the forced-libraries mechanism, but grep over all crates shows zero callers: cmd_play passes env Vec::new() (main.rs:195) and cmd_tool passes only run.env (main.rs:378). The GUI shells out to the same CLI (eidos-gui/src/main.rs:218-226, 282-287).
findings.description: The Linux equivalent of usvfs forced libraries was built and documented but never connected to the pipeline: a mod shipping d3d11.dll/dxgi.dll (ENB, ReShade) or dinput8.dll (.asi loaders) will not load under Proton, because Wine's builtin wins for those names without an explicit n,b override. MO2 applies this on every run as part of beforeRun; Eidos's equivalent hook point is run_through_view's env assembly.
findings.suggested_fix: In run_through_view, scan the enabled mod roots (and Overwrite) for top-level .dll stems that shadow Wine builtins, compose wine_dll_overrides(stems, std::env::var("WINEDLLOVERRIDES").ok().as_deref()), and push it into LaunchSpec.env for both play and tool paths (optionally overridable per tool in tools.ini, matching MO2's per-executable setting).

findings.title: Child killed by a signal is reported as exit code 0 (success)
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/processrunner.cpp:427-443 - waitForProcess always retrieves the real exit code via GetExitCodeProcess into m_exitCode, which is propagated (exitCode(), organizercore.cpp:2044 afterRun receives it and forwards to m_FinishedRun plugins); a crashed child never reads back as success.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos/src/main.rs:236 - 'exit(status.code().unwrap_or(0))': on Unix, ExitStatus::code() is None when the child was terminated by a signal, so a SIGSEGV-crashed or SIGKILLed game/tool makes eidos exit 0.
findings.description: eidos play is designed to sit inside Steam's %command% chain and eidos tool inside scripts; both report success when the wrapped process died from a signal. MO2 always propagates the real exit condition. The shell convention is 128+signal, which Rust exposes via ExitStatusExt.
findings.suggested_fix: use std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt; exit(status.code().unwrap_or_else(|| 128 + status.signal().unwrap_or(1))) in run_through_view.

subsystems.subsystem: game/tool launch pipeline (process construction + before/after hooks)

findings.title: tools.ini args round-trip splits on every space, corrupting arguments that contain spaces
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/executableslist.cpp:99 and :125 store `arguments` as a single string; modorganizer/src/spawn.cpp:442-444 appends that string verbatim to the CreateProcess command line, so embedded quotes preserve spaces. MO2 itself relies on this: executableslist.cpp:155-156 wraps the Explorer++ data-dir argument in quotes (`QString("\"%1\"")`).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/tools.rs:70 writes `args=` as `t.args.join(" ")`; tools.rs:53-54 reads it back with `v.split(' ')`. crates/eidos/src/main.rs:298 stores each shell argv element as one Vec entry, so an arg containing a space survives `add` but is split into multiple argv entries on the next read (every `list`/`run` re-reads tools.ini via inst.tools()).
findings.description: An argument like xEdit's `-D:D:\My Mods\Data` or `-cache:C:\path with spaces` is stored joined with spaces and re-split on every single space, producing broken argv. Doubled spaces also yield empty-string argv entries (`split(' ')` keeps empties). Because the Proton invocation passes argv elements directly (proton.rs:30-37), there is no way for the user to express quoting at all - MO2's single-string + Windows quoting rules handles this.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the args encoding quote-aware: on write, quote any arg containing spaces/quotes (shell-words style escaping); on read, split with those quoting rules instead of `split(' ')`. Alternatively store one `argN=` key per argument, which round-trips losslessly with zero parsing.

findings.title: Proton env lacks SteamAppId / SteamGameId / STEAM_COMPAT_APP_ID, which MO2 always sets and Proton consults
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/spawn.cpp:612-621: before every spawn MO2 sets env `SteamAPPId` from the executable's steamAppID, falling back to the game's configured app ID. The field is a first-class part of the executable model: uibase/src/executableinfo.cpp:60-64 (withSteamAppId), executableslist.cpp:100/:127 (load/store per entry).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-games/src/proton.rs:163-175: ProtonRun.env contains only STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH and STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH; `app_id` is already a parameter of proton_command (proton.rs:153) but never exported. The Eidos Tool model (tools.rs:16-26) has no steam-app-id field either.
findings.description: Verified against the real scripts on this machine: Proton 11 keys per-app workarounds on `SteamAppId` (proton:1234) and `STEAM_COMPAT_APP_ID` (proton:1398), and PROTON_LOG per-game logging silently no-ops without `SteamGameId` (proton:1589-1592); GE-Proton's protonfixes also resolves the game by these vars. Most concretely, Eidos seeds the script-extender loader (skse64_loader.exe) as a default tool (tools.rs:97-110), and SKSE launches the game exe whose steam_api init needs SteamAppId in the environment - exactly the case MO2's env::set("SteamAPPId") exists for.
findings.suggested_fix: In proton_command, extend ProtonRun.env with ("SteamAppId", app_id), ("SteamGameId", app_id) and ("STEAM_COMPAT_APP_ID", app_id) - Steam sets all three for compat launches and app_id is already in scope.

findings.title: Verb 'run' without STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH deletes the prefix's s: gamedrive link on every tool launch; Steam's main-app verb is waitforexitandrun
findings.mo2_evidence: MO2 (Windows) has no Proton verb; the parity targets are (a) MO2 running each tool as the exclusive foreground app and blocking on it (processrunner.cpp:495-507 setWaitForCompletion, :689 run()), and (b) Steam's own invocation contract: 'Proton 11.0/toolmanifest.vdf':4 `"commandline" "/proton %verb%"` with verb=waitforexitandrun for the main app. Verified in the local Proton 11 script: the `run` verb additionally executes setup_game_dir_drive() (proton:2082-2085); `gamedrive` is in the default compat config unconditionally (proton:1396); without STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH/STEAM_COMPAT_LIBRARY_PATHS try_get_game_library_dir() returns None (proton:275-283) and setup_dir_drive then REMOVES dosdevices/s: (proton:296-298). GE-Proton10-34 behaves identically (proton:2398-2402, drive setup also inside prefix update at :1314). `waitforexitandrun` skips the drive teardown and first runs `wineserver -w` (proton:2087-2091).
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-games/src/proton.rs:33 hardcodes the "run" verb in ProtonRun::command; proton.rs:165-174 sets neither STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH nor STEAM_COMPAT_LIBRARY_PATHS. The doc comment (proton.rs:10-11, :21) bakes 'run' in as the design.
findings.description: Two consequences, both verified in the actual Proton scripts: (1) every Eidos tool launch silently deletes the prefix's s: gamedrive symlink (a prefix mutation Steam repairs only on a later launch that re-runs drive setup - tools or saved paths referencing s: break meanwhile); (2) 'run' skips the `wineserver -w` wait, so a tool launched right after the game (or another tool) exits can race a still-dying wineserver from the previous session - the exact scenario waitforexitandrun exists for. Prefix setup itself is NOT skipped by 'run' (init_session runs for both verbs, proton:2079), so that part is fine.
findings.suggested_fix: Switch ProtonRun::command to the "waitforexitandrun" verb - Eidos's tool launch is exclusive (gui main.rs:216-218: 'same single-process requirement as play'), matching Steam's main-app semantics. Additionally pass STEAM_COMPAT_INSTALL_PATH=<game install dir> and STEAM_COMPAT_LIBRARY_PATHS=<library root> (both already known to detection) so any code path that does run gamedrive setup repairs s: instead of deleting it.

findings.title: Tool titles are written unsanitized into the tools.ini section header - a newline corrupts the file
findings.mo2_evidence: modorganizer/src/executableslist.cpp:120 stores the title as a QSettings VALUE (map["title"]), not as a section name, so any character (']', '=', newline) is safe by construction; MO2 needs no sanitization.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-instance/src/tools.rs:68 emits `format!("[Tool/{}]", t.title)`. A title containing a newline (possible via `eidos tool add $'Foo\nBar' ...`, main.rs:288-300 accepts any string) splits the header across two lines; on re-read (tools.rs:36-49) neither line parses as a section, the entry is dropped, and its exe=/args= keys attach to the PREVIOUS tool via out.last_mut(). Titles with leading/trailing whitespace also fail to round-trip because section_header trims the whole inner string (crates/eidos-ini/src/lib.rs:23-26).
findings.description: Round-trip corruption that silently rewrites a neighbouring tool's exe/args on the next save. A lone ']' actually survives (only the outer brackets are stripped), so the practical injection vector is control characters and whitespace edges - but the failure mode (keys re-attached to the wrong tool) is nasty when it happens.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate titles at the `add` boundary and in write_tools: reject empty titles and any title containing control characters (\n, \r), and trim leading/trailing whitespace before writing, mirroring what the format can actually round-trip.

findings.title: `--print` is detected even after the `--` separator, hijacking a literal --print meant for the tool
findings.mo2_evidence: absent - no MO2 analog flag; the relevant contract is MO2's pass-through of user arguments verbatim to the spawned tool (processrunner.cpp:620 setArguments(args.join(" ")) in setFromFileOrExecutable, no flag scanning inside them). The fix belongs in cmd_tool's own arg parsing.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos/src/main.rs:329 `args.iter().any(|a| a == "--print")` scans ALL remaining args, including those after the `--` separator extracted at main.rs:330-333. `eidos tool <id> run <title> -- --print` therefore enters print-only mode instead of forwarding `--print` to the tool, contradicting the documented contract that everything after `--` is extra tool args (usage text, main.rs:262/326).
findings.description: The `--` separator is supposed to make everything after it opaque tool arguments, but the --print scan ignores the boundary. Any tool that itself takes a --print flag cannot receive it.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the `--` position first and only search for "--print" in args[..sep] (the pre-separator slice).

findings.title: Write/delete paths use literal casing while reads fold case: lost deletes, EIO write-opens, split-brain duplicate copies
findings.mo2_evidence: usvfs/src/shared/directory_tree.h:185-231 - the redirection tree's NodeMapT uses CILess (_strnicmp), so every reroute (read, write, delete, create) resolves case-insensitively to the single real node; kernel32.cpp:567-601 (DeleteFileW) and ntdll.cpp:1264-1295 (NtCreateFile) therefore always hit the same real file regardless of the casing the game uses.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-core/src/lib.rs:122-124 resolve_write joins the raw requested casing; :145 open_for_write gates copy-up on exact-case dest.exists(); :184-187 remove() checks dest.is_dir()/dest.exists() exact-case; :47-52 whiteout_path joins raw parent casing. Contrast :102-110 resolve_read and even :128-131 needs_copy_up, which use ci_lookup. FUSE fallout: crates/eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:345-363 + 370-380 (open for write of a case-mismatched overwrite file opens a nonexistent exact-case path without O_CREAT and replies EIO).
findings.description: Eidos advertises Windows case-insensitivity, and Wine trusts it: a stat of 'foo.txt' succeeds on the mount, so Wine issues syscalls with whatever casing the game used. Three concrete failures when the overwrite layer holds 'Foo.txt' and the game asks with 'FOO.TXT'/'foo.txt': (1) unlink: remove() finds no exact-case overwrite copy and no lower copy, returns Ok, file silently survives the delete (DeleteFile succeeds but GetFileAttributes still finds it - impossible under usvfs); (2) open for write: open_for_write returns overwrite/FOO.TXT which does not exist, the read-write open without create fails, game gets EIO on a file that visibly exists; (3) with a lower copy present, open_for_write copies the pristine lower file to a second case-variant overwrite entry, so the game writes to a stale duplicate and ci_lookup's read_dir scan resolves the two variants nondeterministically. make_dir/whiteout_path can similarly create duplicate case-variant directories (overwrite/Data next to overwrite/data), splitting contents.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a case-insensitive write resolver in eidos-core: walk vpath components against the overwrite root with ci_lookup, reusing the existing entry when a CI match exists and only falling back to the requested casing for genuinely new components. Use it in open_for_write, prepare_overwrite, make_dir, remove, rename, and whiteout_path. Add core tests: create 'Foo.txt' in overwrite, then unlink/open-for-write/copy-up via other casings.

findings.title: Renaming a directory with lower-layer content: EIO for lower-only dirs, silent loss of lower children for mixed dirs
findings.mo2_evidence: usvfs/src/usvfs_dll/hooks/kernel32.cpp:774-867 hook_MoveFileExW: detects directories (:803 pathIsDirectory), physically moves the real directory with MoveFileExW (:830) or SHFileOperation across drives (:806-829), then RerouteW::addDirectoryMapping (:843-849) remaps the whole subtree, so every child (including mod-provided files) arrives at the destination.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-core/src/lib.rs:199-219 LayerStack::rename: open_for_write(from) only copies up when src.is_file() (:146-149), so for a lower-only dir fs::rename(:209) runs on a nonexistent overwrite path and errors; for a dir that exists in overwrite AND lower, it renames only the overwrite half and whiteouts 'from' (:211-217). crates/eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:833-869 maps the error to EIO. The doc comment (:201-202) acknowledges 'lower-only directory renames are not yet supported'.
findings.description: Two distinct behaviors, both wrong vs usvfs. (a) Lower-only directory: rename(2) fails with EIO (not even a clean EXDEV), so Wine's MoveFile on a folder that only exists in a mod/game layer hard-fails where MO2 succeeds. (b) Mixed directory (game wrote some files into a dir that also has mod/game files): fs::rename moves only the overwrite children to 'to', then writes a whiteout on 'from', so all lower-layer children vanish from both names. The game believes it renamed a folder with N files and finds a subset - silent data hiding. Concrete risk: any tool or game doing dir-swap updates (rename Data\foo -> Data\foo.bak, profile/cache/backup folder moves under Wine) corrupts the merged view; the EIO variant also breaks installers run inside the mount.
findings.suggested_fix: In LayerStack::rename, detect when the source resolves to a directory in any layer: recursively materialise the MERGED tree (list_dir walk; copy files up, fs::rename overwrite-side entries where possible) into the destination, then whiteout the source dir. Until implemented, at minimum return EXDEV instead of EIO for directory sources so callers with copy fallbacks (MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED, mv) can recover, and reflect both cases in tests/union.rs.

findings.title: mkdir over a whited-out directory clears the whiteout and resurrects previously deleted lower files
findings.mo2_evidence: usvfs/src/usvfs_dll/hooks/kernel32.cpp:567-601 hook_DeleteFileW deletes the real (mod) file and removes the mapping, and :1197-1222 hook_CreateDirectoryW just creates/reroutes a directory - a deleted file can never reappear when its parent directory is removed and re-created, matching NTFS.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-core/src/lib.rs:157-162 make_dir unconditionally clear_whiteout(vpath) for the directory itself; :184-186 remove() of a directory does remove_dir_all on the overwrite copy, destroying the child whiteout markers stored inside it; :250-252 list_dir's opacity depends on exactly the marker make_dir deletes. FUSE path: crates/eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:665-688 mkdir -> make_dir.
findings.description: Sequence: lower layer has dir/a.txt. Game deletes dir\a.txt (whiteout overwrite/dir/.eidoswh.a.txt), then RemoveDirectory(dir) (list_dir is empty so rmdir passes; remove() does remove_dir_all - the a.txt marker is destroyed - and writes .eidoswh.dir), then CreateDirectory(dir) (lookup is hidden so the kernel calls FUSE mkdir; make_dir clears .eidoswh.dir). Now nothing hides dir/a.txt and the deleted file is back in lookups and listings. Under Windows/usvfs a recreated directory is empty. 'Clear cache folder then recreate it' is a common game/installer pattern, and stale loose files resurfacing is exactly the class of bug that breaks modded load orders. The existing recreated_directory_is_opaque test only covers implicit recreation via open_for_write of a child, which does not clear the parent whiteout, so the explicit-mkdir hole is untested.
findings.suggested_fix: When make_dir finds a whiteout on the directory and the directory exists in a lower layer, do not just clear it: replace it with an opaque-directory marker (e.g. .eidoswh_opaque inside the new overwrite dir) honoured by hidden_by_whiteout/list_dir, so lower contents stay hidden. Alternatively, before remove_dir_all in remove(), re-emit per-child whiteouts after recreating... the opaque marker is the simpler invariant. Add a core test for delete-file / rmdir / mkdir / list.

findings.title: Copy-up resets mtime and drops xattrs; usvfs preserves them by writing through to the real file
findings.mo2_evidence: usvfs never copies: ntdll.cpp:1264-1295 reroutes NtCreateFile to the existing real lower file for write/truncate dispositions and operates in place, and kernel32.cpp:546-565 hook_SetFileAttributesW likewise reroutes in place - so file times, DOS attributes, and ADS of a mod file are untouched by opening it for write or setting one attribute.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-core/src/lib.rs:145-151 copy-up is std::fs::copy, which copies contents and permission bits only - the new overwrite file gets mtime=now and loses xattrs (including Wine's user.DOSATTRIB). Triggered by any write-open even if nothing is written (crates/eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:345-354), by setattr for a lone chmod/utimes (:756-775), and by rename's copy-up (lib.rs:204).
findings.description: Opening a lower-layer file with GENERIC_WRITE, chmod-ing it, or renaming it bumps its visible mtime to now and strips Wine-stored DOS attributes, where under MO2/usvfs the timestamps and attributes are exactly the real file's. Creation Engine and tooling (xEdit, Wrye Bash, MO2 itself) compare mtimes for plugin ordering and 'file changed' detection; a spurious mtime=now on copy-up makes pristine mod files look freshly modified and can reorder timestamp-based logic. This is within the deliberate COW design, not a challenge to it: overlayfs solves the same problem by preserving times/xattrs during copy-up.
findings.suggested_fix: After fs::copy in open_for_write (and the rename copy-up), replicate the source's atime/mtime onto the destination (utimensat, like eidos-fuse's set_times helper - move it or a sibling into eidos-core) and copy user.* xattrs (llistxattr/lgetxattr/lsetxattr loop). Exempt the O_TRUNC path if the truncate refinement lands. Pin with a test asserting copied-up files keep the lower file's mtime.

findings.title: O_TRUNC (TRUNCATE_EXISTING/CREATE_ALWAYS) on a lower file copies the full content up before discarding it
findings.mo2_evidence: usvfs/src/usvfs_dll/maptracker.h:597-604 and :617-628 - TRUNCATE_EXISTING truncates the existing file in place (no copy ever happens in usvfs), and when the file only exists virtually-missing it converts the disposition to CREATE_ALWAYS at the create target; overwrite dispositions never pay a content-copy cost.
findings.eidos_evidence: crates/eidos-fuse/src/lib.rs:346-354 open() calls stack.open_for_write before inspecting flags, so eidos-core lib.rs:145-151 fs::copy duplicates the entire lower file into overwrite, then :383-385 immediately set_len(0) throws the bytes away.
findings.description: Every CreateFile(CREATE_ALWAYS/TRUNCATE_EXISTING) a game issues on a large lower-layer file (log rewrites, cache regeneration, tools rewriting plugins or archives) pays a full read+write of the old content for nothing - on a multi-GB archive that is seconds of stall and double disk traffic at game-visible latency. The end state (empty overwrite file shadowing the lower copy, whiteout cleared) is reachable without the copy.
findings.suggested_fix: In Eidos::open(), when want_write and O_TRUNC is set, use stack.prepare_overwrite (which already creates parents and clears whiteouts without copying) and open with create(true).truncate(true); optionally clone permissions/xattrs from the lower file to keep the metadata-preservation story consistent. Add a union.rs test that truncating a lower file does not read it.
